name: ISNUMBER
description: ISNUMBER returns TRUE if the supplied value is a number (including numeric results of formulas and dates stored as serial numbers), and FALSE otherwise.
tldr: Tests whether a value is numeric.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value, cell reference, or formula result to test.

basicExample.description: Check a cell that holds a number
basicExample.explanation: A1 contains 100, which is numeric, so the function returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: Text that looks like a number
advancedExamples.scenario: A cell shows 007 but it is stored as text.
advancedExamples.explanation: "123" in quotes is text, not a numeric value, so the result is FALSE.

advancedExamples.title: Validate a column of entries
advancedExamples.scenario: Flag rows whose ID is not numeric.
advancedExamples.description: Combine with IF to label bad data
advancedExamples.explanation: If B2 holds non-numeric text, ISNUMBER returns FALSE and IF returns "fix".

howItWorks: ISNUMBER inspects the data type of the supplied value. Numeric types (numbers, formula results that are numbers, and dates stored as serial numbers) return TRUE; everything else—text, logicals, errors, blank cells—returns FALSE. A text string that merely resembles a number is not numeric.

howToSteps.name: Pick the value
howToSteps.text: Choose the cell or value you want to test.

howToSteps.name: Read the result
howToSteps.text: TRUE means numeric, FALSE means not.

limitations: Returns FALSE for text that looks like a number, such as "123".
A blank cell returns FALSE because blank is not a number.
Dates are numbers, so ISNUMBER returns TRUE for date values.

commonErrors.cause: The value is a number stored as text.
commonErrors.fix: Convert it to a real number with VALUE() or Text to Columns.
Use ISBLANK if you specifically need to test for emptiness.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISNUMBER works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: Does ISNUMBER recognize dates?
faq.answer: Yes, because dates are stored as serial numbers, so they return TRUE.

faq.question: Why does ISNUMBER("123") return FALSE?
faq.answer: Because "123" in quotes is text, not a numeric value.

faq.question: Can I test a whole range at once?
faq.answer: ISNUMBER tests a single value; wrap it in an array-aware function, e.g. =SUMPRODUCT(--ISNUMBER(A1:A10)) to count numeric cells.
